description: Task attributes: on a task item's first line (a list item with a box, `[c]` and a space or tab after it, in a quote too), `>YYYY-MM-DD` is a due date and `@` straight before `[[Title]]` is a parent, each at the text's start or after a space or tab (no other whitespace). The first of each counts; a later one is text. The scan runs over the text after the box and skips code spans and links (`[[…]]`, `![[…]]`, `[text](target)` and `[text][ref]`: the text's brackets nest, a backslash escapes one, the target's parentheses balance); emphasis, `~~`, `==` and math are read through. Each attribute's `column` and `length` place it in its line (UTF-16 units). Plain list items and paragraphs hold none; `>` at a line's start is a quote.

due.start: `>` at the text's start or after a space or tab
due.date: YYYY-MM-DD, a real calendar date, year 0001 to 9999 (the leap day only in a leap year)
due.end: the line's end, or a character that isn't a letter or digit (`>2026-10-09-draft` and `>2026-10-09,` count; `>2026-10-091` doesn't)

parent.start: `@` at the text's start or after a space or tab, immediately followed by `[[`
parent.length: `@` through `]]`; the link holds no `[` or `]` and links a file (`[[#heading]]` and `[[]]` don't)
parent.value: the link's title: its target's last path component without `.md` (folder, heading, block and alias dropped); the link is also in `links`

typing.dateQuery: `>` after whitespace on a task line opens a query: letters, digits, `-`, `/` and at most two single spaces; any other character, a space straight after `>` or past 40 characters ends it
typing.parentQuery: `@` after whitespace on a task line opens a query (also `@[[`): any text but newline, `[`, `]`, `|`, `#` and `^`, not starting with a space, up to 100 characters
